entry.title: Optimal Trading Speed on Blockchain
entry.summary:
On blockchain-based exchanges, faster blocks weaken the priority-fee competition among arbitrageurs and shift rents from the block producer to them. Equilibrium liquidity peaks at an interior block speed; beyond a threshold, an active liquidity provider cream-skims and passive capital shrinks. Evidence from the Base Flashblocks upgrade, a tenfold block-speed increase, confirms the predictions.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance

entry.title: Choosing Complexity: Cognitive Ability, Overconfidence, and Task Choice. Workers and organizations routinely choose between complex tasks that differ in their success-payment tradeoff.
entry.summary:
Workers and organizations routinely choose between complex tasks that differ in their success-payment tradeoff. We study how cognitive ability and overconfidence shape this choice of task complexity, both theoretically and experimentally. Consistent with our model, we find that more cognitively able individuals choose more complex tasks.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #market-design #decision-theory

entry.title: Dynamic investment and coordination in teams: Theory and experimental evidence
entry.summary:
Teamwork requires more than the general skills that team members bring. In successful teams, members invest in team-specific skill or capital that accumulates within the team and raises the return to coordinated production. We provide the first systematic analysis of dynamic investment in such team skill.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory

entry.title: Target What? The Foundations of Poverty Targeting -- by Rema Hanna, Emily Breza, Benjamin A. Olken, Abhijit Banerjee, Arun G. Chandrasekhar, Gideon Moore
entry.summary:
Most government transfer programs aim to target the poor. Doing so implicitly assumes that the lowest-consumption households have the highest marginal social valuation, i.e., have the highest social welfare gain from an additional dollar. But this need not be the case.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: Unconventional Monetary Policy and Deposit Retention -- by Philip Strahan, Tuo Yang
entry.summary:
The two dimensions of unconventional monetary policy — holding the short rate at the zero-lower bound (ZLB) and quantitative easing (QE) — shifted deposit composition toward more interest-sensitive customers. The ZLB drew these customers by creating rate compression, which limited the benefit of searching for high-yielding liquidity sources. QE also drew rate-sensitive, large depositors from the Federal Reserve’s purchases of bonds from non-banks.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: Debiasing Law Enforcement Officers: Evidence from an Expressive Arts Intervention in India -- by Sofia Amaral, Girija Borker, Nishith Prakash, María Micaela Sviatschi
entry.summary:
Frontline state agents exercise substantial discretion over citizens’ access to public services, yet little is known about whether the attitudes and beliefs shaping this discretion can be changed among incumbent bureaucrats. Partnering with the Bihar Police - one of India’s largest states that operates under comparatively severe policing capacity constraints, we conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial across 417 police stations and roughly 2,500 active duty senior field police officers to evaluate a three-day expressive arts intervention, grounded in the Theatre of the Oppressed, designed to change police responses to gender-based violence (GBV). Approximately 7 months after baseline, treated officers exhibit more favorable attitudes toward GBV, greater empathy, and stronger legal knowledge.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #infosec #agents

entry.title: TaskNet: Building Occupational Task Inventories from Worker Interviews at Scale -- by Jennifer Wang, Andreas Haupt, Isaac Robinson, Phil Lewis, Erik Brynjolfsson, Diyi Yang
entry.summary:
Understanding how AI is reshaping work requires an accurate account of the tasks workers perform. Workers are often the first to see how their jobs are changing, as new responsibilities and tools often appear in everyday work before these changes reach formal descriptions. Interviews with workers can help capture these emerging changes in job tasks.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #databases

entry.title: The Hidden Sharpe Ratio -- by Mikhail Chernov, Bryan T. Kelly, Semyon Malamud, Johannes Schwab
entry.summary:
We estimate the maximal Sharpe ratio in large cross-sections of assets directly, without constructing the efficient portfolio. Covariance estimation in this setting requires regularization, which suppresses the contribution of small-eigenvalue directions. Our estimator progressively recovers this contribution, yielding tight upper and lower bounds with asymptotic confidence intervals.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals -- by Ginger Zhe Jin, Liad Wagman, Jingyi Xing
entry.summary:
We study California's short-term lodging price transparency law (AB 537), which from July 1, 2024 required Airbnb and other providers to advertise fee-inclusive prices. Using Coarsened Exact Matching to compare Airbnb listings in San Diego and San Francisco with those in Seattle and Chicago, we find that all-in pricing made guests more price-sensitive relative to control cities; yet, contrary to the standard prediction that transparency lowers prices, average daily rates rose by 4.8 percent. We also observe significant market churn: relative to control cities, treated cities saw more exits and entries, listings reliant on cleaning-fee revenue disproportionately exited, higher-quality listings were more likely to stay, and entrants offered lower fees and lower quality than incumbents.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #distributed-systems
